# `toolu rust-quality`

Rust quality rules for reviews and the push gate.

Owner: `plugins/rust-quality`.

## `toolu rust-quality`

```text
rust-quality no longer runs after every edit; its SessionStart hook retires any earlier registration. toolu rust-quality check runs the blocking rules over a whole repository (or the paths you name). Blocking findings (inline test modules, misplaced tests, lint suppression, unsafe code, unwrap/expect/panic in src, mocks) fail the file's quality-gate entry; a failing gate denies git push while gates.qualityGate blocks — commits are never stopped. Oversized files, functions and impl blocks and missing or verbose docs advise and never block.

Limits come from lang.rust in toolu.config.json (maxFileLines, maxFnLines, maxImplLines, noMocks); crates allowed to use unsafe are listed in settings/rust-unsafe-exemptions.txt.

Usage: toolu rust-quality [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  check  Run the blocking Rust quality rules over a repository's .rs files
  help   Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --json
          Print exactly one JSON document on stdout

  -q, --quiet
          Drop the diagnostics of a successful run

      --host <HOST>
          The host to act for, instead of the detected one

          [possible values: claude, codex, cursor, grok, hermes, muse, opencode, qwen]

      --config-dir <DIR>
          Read the toolu config from DIR instead of the host's default

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `toolu rust-quality check`

```text
Run the blocking Rust quality rules over every tracked or untracked, not ignored .rs file under the paths (the whole repository by default), with the limits of lang.rust in toolu.config.json. Prints one block per finding. Exits 1 with findings or when git fails, 69 without ast-grep.

Usage: toolu rust-quality check [OPTIONS] [PATH]...

Arguments:
  [PATH]...
          Directories or files to check, relative to the working directory

Options:
      --json
          Print exactly one JSON document on stdout

  -q, --quiet
          Drop the diagnostics of a successful run

      --host <HOST>
          The host to act for, instead of the detected one

          [possible values: claude, codex, cursor, grok, hermes, muse, opencode, qwen]

      --config-dir <DIR>
          Read the toolu config from DIR instead of the host's default

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```
